perspective:
**Alice Lim’s accessible information / subjective reconstruction:**

- Alice knows she is a dental hygienist. She knows Austin Moreno is an old, close friend from high school; they have different career paths and often discuss personal/professional lives and support each other.
- She has observed Austin becoming reserved when they talk about work. She suspects he might be hiding something about his job performance, feels concerned/curious, and invites him to coffee.
- In their first conversation, Alice asks if everything is okay at the office. She hears Austin say it is “nothing really,” just “usual ups and downs,” but also that he is not sure how to handle a few things at work and that it is complicated.
- Alice then believes Austin may be considering a career change because of work dissatisfaction. She feels worried and decides to share her healthcare experience and discuss possible career paths.
- She asks Austin if he has thought about changing careers and says a fresh start can be good. She hears Austin say he has thought about it but does not know what other paths he could take, and he asks for her suggestion. She tells him healthcare needs dedicated people and offers to tell him more and connect him with contacts. She hears Austin say that sounds interesting and that he wants to know more about her experiences and what it involves.
- Alice senses Austin is hesitant about changing careers because he fears the unknown. She feels frustration and empathy, and tells him about her friend Lara, who switched to healthcare in her late 30s and is happier. She hears Austin say this is inspiring but that he worries about risks and the initial struggle. Alice tells him that is natural, growth comes from stepping out of comfort zones, and she is there to support him. She hears Austin thank her and say it helps to have her support and hear real success stories.
- Seeing Austin’s openness, Alice feels encouraged and hopeful. She offers to connect him with a career counselor and friends in healthcare. She hears Austin say that would be helpful and that he appreciates the connections. She says it is about taking first steps and that she will set up a meeting next week. She hears Austin thank her and say he is looking forward to it.
- After several discussions and meetings she participated in, Alice believes Austin is ready to take next steps and appreciates her help. She feels satisfaction and joy and plans regular check-ins. She tells Austin she is proud of the steps he has taken and asks how he feels. She hears Austin say he feels excited, a bit nervous, and mostly grateful for her help. She suggests regular check-ins and hears Austin agree, saying it will keep him focused and that he values her perspective.

She does not have access to Austin’s unspoken private thoughts, narrator-only labels, or events she did not observe/hear/participate in.
